{"answer":"
Drooling in a healthy toddler is often normal and can go with teething
, and 
so can chewing, fussiness and sore, swollen gums
. 
A cold teething ring or a clean finger rubbed on the gums can help.
","triage":"Call 811 if there's a fever, crying you can't settle, trouble swallowing, or they seem ill, because <cite index=\"4-2\">teething doesn't cause fever</cite>. Call 911 now if the drooling is sudden, or if they can't speak, are choking, or have trouble breathing.","sources":["HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics)","Children's Hospital of Philadelphia","St. Louis Children's Hospital","Children's Hospital Los Angeles"]}
